answers.answer: Each player starts with 25 money, 1 active worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers below it, draws 8 Zoo cards and keeps 4 (discarding 4), and draws 2 hidden Final Scoring cards. Each player puts Animals side I in the leftmost slot (strength 1); the other four side-I Action cards are randomly placed in the remaining slots. Appeal starts at 0 for the first player, then 1, 2, and 3 by turn order.
answers.evidence: Take 25 money; draw 2 Final Scoring cards; draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4. Place one card side I up ... Animals card under the leftmost slot. Appeal ... start player on space 0, second ... 1, third ... 2, fourth ... 3.

answers.answer: Four players place the top 4 Base Conservation Project cards face up below the Association board; games with 2 or 3 players place the top 3. Only in a 2-player game, block the left level on the left project, middle level on the middle project, right level on the right project, and the three spaces in the donation area's left column; neither player may use them. The initial 6-card display is revealed only after everyone has chosen their starting hand cards.
answers.evidence: In a 4-player game place the 4 topmost face up below the board; otherwise the 3 topmost. 2-player game only ... cover ... [listed levels and donation spaces]. After everyone has chosen their hand cards, reveal the 6 cards of the display.

answers.answer: After using a card in slot 4, remove it, shift the cards that were left of the empty slot one space right, and put the used card in slot 1. Set action strength before performing the action; each X-token spent adds +1 strength and returns to the supply, and X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost it. You may hold at most 5 X-tokens. An after-finishing effect happens after completing the action, including moving the Action cards.
answers.evidence: After completing the action ... shift all Action cards left of the now-empty slot one slot to the right, and place the used card in slot 1. You set the strength before performing the action ... can never hold more than 5 X-tokens.

answers.answer: You may not take a regular action that does nothing; instead, if you cannot or do not want to perform one of the five actions, choose an Action card, take exactly 1 X-token, move that card to slot 1, and shift the intervening cards right. The slot strength and upgrade side do not matter. You cannot take this alternative action while holding 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: You may not do nothing ... Use the alternative X-token action. ... take exactly 1 X-token ... move it to slot 1 and shift the intervening cards right ... If you already have 5 X-tokens, you cannot perform this action.

answers.answer: When the Break token reaches its last space, ignore any additional steps beyond that space and the player who reached it gains 1 X-token. The break occurs after that player's current turn ends, so they finish the turn; then the break procedure happens, and play continues clockwise with the next player.
answers.evidence: When it reaches the last space ... break takes place after the end of your current turn, and you get 1 X-token ... Ignore any additional steps beyond the last space. ... Play then continues clockwise with the next player.

answers.answer: Both sides advance the Break token 2 spaces. On side I, choose either a deck draw using the strength table (up to 3 cards, with any required discard) or snap exactly 1 display card at strength 5+, regardless of reputation and without drawing from the deck. On side II, draw from the deck and/or from within reputation range in any order using the side-II table, or snap exactly 1 display card at strength 3+; a snap ignores reputation and has no deck draw. Display cards are replenished only after the turn is complete. There is no in-turn hand limit; discard down to the limit at breaks.
answers.evidence: Side I ... Advance the Break token 2 spaces ... either draw from the deck ... or snap ... strength 5 or more. Side II: Advance ... 2 spaces ... deck and/or from within reputation range ... Snapping now works from strength 3 ... display is not replenished until your turn is complete ... discard to your limit during breaks.

answers.answer: Reputation range includes the display card on the folder matching your Reputation counter and every lower-numbered folder. Reputation 10 or higher requires the upgraded Cards action. At reputation 15, additional reputation does not move the counter; gain 1 appeal for each further reputation step. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: ‘Within reputation range’ = the display card on the folder matching your counter plus all lower-numbered folders. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action. If your counter is on space 15 ... 1 appeal per remaining reputation step. You may not look through the discard pile.

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building of size up to strength; Build II builds any number of different buildings with total size no greater than strength, never two identical buildings in the same action. Pay 2 money per space before placing each building. The first building must have at least one space on a map border; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. Build only on empty spaces, without extending past the map, overlapping buildings, or covering water/rock; restricted-icon spaces require Build II. Kiosks must be at least 3 spaces apart. Each pavilion immediately gives 1 appeal, once.
answers.evidence: Build exactly 1 building ... Pay 2 money per space ... first building ... border space ... build adjacent to an existing building ... restricted icon require[s] the upgraded Build action. A kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk ... Each pavilion ... increases ... appeal by 1.

answers.answer: Build I can build kiosks, pavilions, standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), and one Petting Zoo per zoo (size 3). Build II additionally allows the Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary (size 5 each); each of the three special enclosure types has a one-per-zoo limit. The component list has 4 of each special enclosure type. Unique buildings cannot be built with the Build action and enter through Sponsor cards. Covering every map space except water and rock immediately grants 7 appeal.
answers.evidence: Available [on Build I] ... Petting Zoo ... maximum 1 per zoo. ... Reptile House and Large Bird Aviary ... maximum 1 each per zoo. Components: 4× Petting Zoo, 4× Reptile House, 4× Large Bird Aviary. Unique buildings can never be built with this action ... full map ... gain 7 appeal.

answers.answer: Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards, and newly activated workers, may be used later in that action. Resolve items one at a time and pay each item before receiving its own benefits. Immediate placement bonuses are taken before building the next building; other ordinary effects resolve immediately unless marked after finishing, which waits until the whole action is complete (and, for the general rule, after moving the Action cards). When effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps ... You must pay each item before receiving its own benefits. ... take placement bonuses before building the next building, but hold ‘after finishing’ bonuses ... Multiple simultaneous effects ... choose the order.

answers.answer: To play an animal, meet all left-side conditions, pay its cost, house it in a legal empty enclosure, place its card, and resolve its effects. A partner zoo matching the animal's continent reduces cost by 3 money for each continent icon on the animal card, including doubled icons. Standard enclosures must be empty and at least the required size; flip one to its occupied side. Any animal except a Petting Zoo animal can use a standard enclosure; Petting Zoo animals can only use the Petting Zoo. Some animals need one or two distinct adjacent water/rock hexes. Reptiles and some birds may use their special enclosure if eligible; mark the animal's indicated number of spaces with player tokens, and it cannot fit if insufficient spaces remain. Special enclosures are not flipped. Ordinary effects resolve immediately, while after-finishing effects wait until the whole Animals action is done and the Animals card is moved; simultaneous effects may be ordered by the player.
answers.evidence: Check conditions ... Pay the cost ... reduces the cost by 3 money per continent icon ... Fill an empty enclosure ... required size ... Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo ... water and/or rock ... mark the number of spaces ... ‘After finishing’ effects wait until the entire Animals action is done.

answers.answer: Animals II adds the option to play eligible animals from the display within reputation range, paying the card's folder number as an extra cost; hand and display animals may be mixed. At strength 5 or more, you may first gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, so the increased range applies. Display cards are not replenished until the turn ends. Animals with the upgrade-required condition icon may be played with Animals II.
answers.evidence: Side II: You may also play Animal cards from the display within your reputation range, paying an additional cost equal to the folder number ... strength 5 or more ... first increase your reputation by 1 ... at the very beginning ... display is not replenished until your turn ends ... may also play animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon.

answers.answer: Only immediately when building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary, and only once per building, may suitable animals be moved from standard enclosures into it. Eligible animals are reptiles and the birds whose cards allow that special enclosure; move only animals that fit the remaining special-enclosure capacity, marking the number of spaces shown on each card with player tokens. For each animal moved, flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all its requirements, including water/rock; if none does, use the smallest occupied enclosure meeting its size requirement; if none meets even size, flip no standard enclosure. Decide separately for each animal.
answers.evidence: When you build the Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary you may immediately — and only once per building — move suitable animals ... To house an animal in a special enclosure, mark the number of spaces shown on the card with player tokens ... flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure that meets all its requirements ... else ... size ... else ... flip none ... decide per animal.

answers.answer: The four task strengths are: increase reputation 2, gain a partner zoo 3, gain a university 4, and conservation project work 5. Association I performs exactly one task. Association II may perform one or more different tasks whose total value is at most the action strength; each task uses 1 or 2 of your workers as required. A task with one of your workers already on it requires placing 2 workers; if 3 of your workers are already there, you cannot do it again until after the break. Other players' workers do not matter.
answers.evidence: Each task has a strength number ... reputation (strength 2) ... partner zoo (strength 3) ... university (strength 4) ... conservation project work (strength 5). Side I ... exactly one ... If 1 of your workers is already on that task, you must place 2 ... if 3 ... cannot ... Other players' workers ... do not matter. Side II ... different ... total value ... may not exceed ... strength.

answers.answer: Partner zoos and universities are taken from the Association board and placed on the lowest available matching spaces on the player's map; their printed bonuses are taken immediately. At breaks, replenish them so each is available exactly once, skipping types all players already have. Partner zoos must be from different continents, with at most 4; a third or fourth requires Association II. Universities cannot be duplicates. Universities are the only way to raise the hand limit from 3 to 5. A bonus that grants a zoo or university takes an available tile from the Association board, not directly from general supply.
answers.evidence: take a partner zoo from the Association board onto the lowest empty ... space (take any printed bonus immediately) ... all ... different continents, maximum 4 ... third (or fourth) requires ... upgraded Association ... cannot take a duplicate university ... Universities ... only way to increase your hand limit to 5. FAQ: bonus ... takes an available Association-board tile.

answers.answer: Base Conservation Projects are set up below the Association board; a Conservation Project card from hand can enter above the board when chosen as conservation project work, and it is supported immediately. Association II can instead play a new project from the in-range display for its folder-number cost. To support a project, meet an unoccupied condition and place one player token from the left edge of your map on it; each player may support each project only once. Taking the token activates its map bonus immediately, either before or after the project reward at the player's choice. If adding a project exceeds the player-count limit, discard the rightmost card and return tokens on it to their owners' supplies; the activated bonuses stay active. Base projects remain below and are never moved, even if fully supported.
answers.evidence: support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately ... To support ... place 1 player token ... each project only once ... bonus ... immediately ... before or after ... If the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card and return ... Base Conservation Projects below the board are never moved.

answers.answer: A release project's printed standard-enclosure size must match exactly; smaller or larger does not qualify. Discarding the animal loses only its printed appeal and its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal, and earlier effects already earned. Remove its special-enclosure tokens first if it could live in a special enclosure and those tokens can be removed; otherwise flip the smallest occupied standard enclosure meeting all requirements (including terrain), or, if none does, the smallest occupied one meeting size alone; if none meets size, flip none. The animal is discarded, thereby freeing the applicable enclosure space.
answers.evidence: required standard size must match exactly, not be smaller or larger. First lose only the animal's printed appeal ... discard the animal and lose its icons. Keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated appeal and earlier effects ... remove ... special-enclosure tokens if possible; only otherwise flip a standard enclosure ... fallback ...

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly 1 Sponsor from hand if strength is at least its level and conditions are met. Sponsors II may play one or more cards if strength +1 is at least their total levels; cards resolve one after another, with instant effects (except after-finishing effects) completed before the next. Side II cards may come from hand or from the display within reputation range, with the folder number paid as an additional cost; refill waits until turn end. Instead of playing Sponsors, either side may advance the Break token by the action strength and take that much money; side II doubles the money. The money is the full amount even if fewer steps remain before the end of the Break track.
answers.evidence: Side I ... exactly 1 Sponsor ... strength ... at least ... level ... OR ... advance ... steps equal to strength and take that much money ... full money even if ... doesn't need all the steps. Side II ... strength +1 ... sum of levels ... hand or display ... paying folder number ... If ... advance the Break token, you take the money twice.

answers.answer: Break order: discard down to the hand limit (3, or 5 with the specified university); return Multiplier, Venom, and Constriction tokens from Action cards; recall workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1 and 2, slide the rest down, and refill; take income; reset the Break token. Income includes appeal-track money, kiosk income, then break-income icons on Sponsor cards and activated zoo-map bonuses. Each kiosk earns 1 money for each adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; an empty standard enclosure does not count, while an empty special enclosure does. If multiple players take display cards during income, refill after each player; effects usually resolve simultaneously, but if order is needed begin with the break initiator (or the affected player closest to them) and proceed clockwise.
answers.evidence: Break procedure ... hand card limit ... tokens ... association board ... replenish display ... take income ... appeal ... kiosk income ... break-income icon ... when multiple players take display cards, refill the display after each player; usually simultaneous ... begin with the player who initiated the break ... proceed clockwise.

answers.answer: At 2 conservation, choose either to upgrade an Action card or activate an additional worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or the Bonus token at that space. The first time anyone reaches 10, all players discard one Final Scoring card; if nobody reaches 10 before the end, all discard one before scoring. Check the end at the end of a player's own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained during another player's turn waits until your own turn ends or a break unless another player triggers the end first. The triggering player completes their turn; then every other player gets one final turn, or if triggered during a break, every player gets one final turn. Each Final Scoring card can grant at most 4 conservation points. Victory Points equal Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing the Conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; ties go to the player with most conservation-project supports, then tied players share the win.
answers.evidence: 2 conservation points: either upgrade ... or activate ... 5 and 8 ... 5 money or ... Bonus token. 10 ... all players ... discard ... End ... at the end of your own turn or during a break ... same scoring area, or pass ... Appeal gained during another player's turn ... waits ... triggering player completes their turn ... one more turn ... during a break, all players ... Final Scoring ... never ... more than 4 ... Victory Points = Appeal value − Target Number ... Tiebreaker ... most ... projects ... share the victory.
